label: ANALOGY PRACTICE
def: To gather or collect a large amount over time.
ex: He amassed a huge collection of stamps.
note: Suggests accumulation, not a single act.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: To officially confirm that something is true or meets a standard.
ex: The inspector certified that the building was safe.
note: Related noun: certificate, the document that certifies.

label: ANALOGY PRACTICE
def: To make something clearer or easier to understand.
ex: The teacher clarified the difficult passage.
note: Noun: clarification.

label: ANALOGY PRACTICE
def: To become smaller or shorter.
ex: Most metals contract slightly as they cool down.
note: Also, to catch an illness; noun: a formal agreement.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: To completely destroy a building or an argument.
ex: The old factory was demolished last year.
note: Noun: demolition.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: To notice or understand something that is not obvious.
ex: It was hard to discern his true motives.
note: Adjective: discerning, showing good judgment.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: To mix into a liquid until it disappears.
ex: Stir the sugar until it dissolves completely in the tea.
note: Also, to end officially: to dissolve a parliament. A substance that dissolves is soluble.

label: ANALOGY PRACTICE
def: To let liquid fall in small drops; in sports, to move a ball with small touches.
ex: The baby dribbled milk down his chin.
note: A slow, small flow, like trickle.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: To turn from liquid into vapor; to disappear gradually.
ex: His enthusiasm evaporated after the first failure.
note: Contrast with condense.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: To bring a feeling or memory to mind.
ex: The song evoked memories of her childhood.
note: Related adjective: evocative.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: Having a wide range of effects or influence.
ex: The new reform had far-reaching consequences for every school.
note: Often said of changes, effects, or decisions.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: To strengthen, especially against attack.
ex: The soldiers fortified the town walls.
note: Related noun: fortification.

label: ANALOGY PRACTICE
def: To gather information bit by bit; originally, to collect leftover grain.
ex: We gleaned a few facts from the old letters.
note: The information is usually gathered slowly or with effort.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: To give or allow something, especially officially.
ex: The bank granted him a loan.
note: To take for granted: to assume without questioning.

label: ANALOGY PRACTICE
def: To put something completely in a liquid; also, to involve deeply.
ex: She immersed herself in her studies.
note: Noun: immersion, as in language immersion.

label: ANALOGY PRACTICE
def: To make laws.
ex: Parliament legislated to protect children from dangerous work.
note: Legislate is to law as compose is to music.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: To investigate or examine closely.
ex: The committee probed the causes of the accident.
note: Also a noun: an investigation or a device for exploring.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: To control something by rules or adjust it to work properly.
ex: The law regulates how factories dispose of waste.
note: Noun: regulation.

label: ANALOGY PRACTICE
def: To move back or withdraw, especially from danger.
ex: The army retreated after heavy losses.
note: Also a quiet place for rest.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: To make holy, or to give something official or moral approval.
ex: The ceremony was meant to sanctify the new temple.
note: Related noun: sanctity; compare sanctuary, a holy or safe place.

label: ANALOGY PRACTICE
def: The liquid that carries food through a plant.
ex: Maple syrup is made from tree sap.
note: As a verb, to gradually weaken: the heat sapped her energy.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: Secretly making clever, dishonest plans to get what one wants.
ex: The scheming adviser plotted to replace the king.
note: From scheme; carries a negative sense, unlike simply planning.

label: ANALOGY PRACTICE
def: Extremely hot, enough to burn.
ex: The scorching sun dried the fields within days.
note: A stronger degree of hot or warm.

label: READING
def: Sacred writings of a religion.
ex: The monks spent hours studying ancient scripture.
note: Often plural: the scriptures.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: A person who travels by sea, especially a sailor.
ex: Early seafarers navigated by the stars.
note: Related adjective: seafaring.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: Experienced through long practice.
ex: A seasoned reporter knows which questions to ask.
note: Of food, it means flavored with salt or spices.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: To break suddenly into many small pieces.
ex: The glass shattered when it hit the floor.
note: Figuratively, hopes or confidence can also be shattered.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: To lose or get rid of something naturally.
ex: Many trees shed their leaves in autumn.
note: Also in "shed light on": to help explain.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: To postpone or set aside a plan.
ex: The company shelved the project due to lack of funds.
note: Postponed, not necessarily cancelled forever.

label: ANALOGY PRACTICE
def: A utensil with a mesh for separating fine particles from coarse ones.
ex: She poured the flour through a sieve.
note: A tool and its action: a sieve is used to sift.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: Treating something complex as if it were much simpler than it is.
ex: His simplistic explanation ignored several key factors.
note: Negative; contrast with simple, which can be positive.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: To read quickly to get the main idea.
ex: She skimmed the article before the meeting.
note: Also, to remove something from a liquid's surface.

label: ANALOGY PRACTICE
def: A person who hates spending money; a miser.
ex: The old skinflint refused to pay for repairs.
note: Stronger and more negative than frugal.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: Unimportant or operating on a minor scale.
ex: He was only a small-time thief, not a gang leader.
note: Contrast with big-time.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: To extract metal from ore by heating and melting it.
ex: Ancient workers smelted copper in simple furnaces.
note: Not to be confused with smelt, a past form of smell.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: To make or become solid, firm, or fixed.
ex: The lava solidified as it cooled.
note: Figuratively, to strengthen: to solidify an alliance.

label: ANALOGY PRACTICE
def: Able to be dissolved in a liquid.
ex: Salt is soluble in water, but sand is not.
note: A problem can also be soluble, meaning solvable; opposite: insoluble.

label: ANALOGY PRACTICE
def: A musical composition for one or two instruments, usually in several movements.
ex: The pianist performed a sonata by Mozart.
note: A type of musical work, as a sonnet is a type of poem.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: The general mood and ideas typical of a particular period.
ex: Her novels captured the spirit of the times.
note: Also known by the German word zeitgeist.

label: ANALOGY PRACTICE
def: To make popping, spitting sounds, or to speak in a confused, hurried way.
ex: The old engine sputtered and then stopped.
note: Splutter is a close variant.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: To waste money, time, or opportunities foolishly.
ex: He squandered his savings on useless gadgets.
note: Contrast with conserve or save.

label: ANALOGY PRACTICE
def: To speak with pauses and repeated sounds, often from nervousness.
ex: He stammered an apology to the angry customer.
note: Close in meaning to stutter.

label: READING
def: Making things conform to one common standard.
ex: Standardization of parts made repairs much easier.
note: Verb: standardize.

label: ANALOGY PRACTICE
def: A group of lines forming a unit in a poem.
ex: The poem has four stanzas of six lines each.
note: Stanza is to poem as paragraph is to essay.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: To encourage activity, growth, or interest.
ex: The new policy aims to stimulate the economy.
note: Related nouns: stimulus, stimulation.

label: ANALOGY PRACTICE
def: To pass a liquid through a sieve to separate solids.
ex: Strain the pasta before adding the sauce.
note: Also, to stretch or overwork: to strain a muscle.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: To make great efforts to achieve something.
ex: The team strives for excellence in every game.
note: Past forms: strove, striven.

label: ANALOGY PRACTICE
def: To speak with involuntary repetition of sounds, especially first sounds.
ex: She stuttered when asked to speak in public.
note: Often a lasting speech condition; compare stammer.

label: READING
def: To put or keep under water.
ex: The flood submerged the entire village.
note: Opposite: emerge or surface.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: To become less strong or intense; to die down.
ex: The storm finally subsided after midnight.
note: Also, of land, to sink to a lower level.

label: READING
def: To stay alive by means of a particular food or income.
ex: The villagers subsisted on rice and fish.
note: Related noun: subsistence, having just enough to survive.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: Small and hard to notice, but important.
ex: There is a subtle difference between the two words.
note: The b is silent; noun: subtlety.

label: ANALOGY PRACTICE
def: The highest point of a mountain.
ex: The climbers reached the summit at dawn.
note: Also, a meeting between heads of government.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: To stop something by force or to hold back a feeling.
ex: She suppressed a laugh during the lecture.
note: Related noun: suppression.

label: READING
def: To overcome a difficulty or obstacle.
ex: They surmounted many problems to finish on time.
note: Related adjective: insurmountable, impossible to overcome.

label: READING
def: To support or keep something going over time.
ex: The river sustains the farms along its banks.
note: Related adjective: sustainable.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: To publicly adopt a position on an issue.
ex: The mayor took a firm stance against the plan.
note: Stance is a position or attitude.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: To become established and begin to grow or develop.
ex: The new ideas slowly took root in society.
note: Literally said of plants; figuratively of ideas and habits.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: Real and able to be touched or clearly seen.
ex: The program produced tangible results within a year.
note: Opposite: intangible.

label: READING
def: To bring something to an end.
ex: The company terminated the contract early.
note: Related noun: termination.

label: READING
def: The set of special terms used in a particular field.
ex: Doctors should avoid technical terminology when speaking to patients.
note: Not to be confused with termination.

label: READING
def: Having a healing or calming effect.
ex: Gardening can be therapeutic for stressed people.
note: Related noun: therapy.

label: ANALOGY PRACTICE
def: A small cap worn on the finger to protect it when sewing.
ex: She pushed the needle through with a thimble.
note: A protective tool, like a helmet for the head.

label: ANALOGY PRACTICE
def: Wood prepared for use in building.
ex: The cabin was built from local timber.
note: Tree is to timber as raw material is to processed material.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: Without success; with no useful result.
ex: They searched for the key, but to no avail.
note: Avail means use or benefit.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: To work very hard for a long time.
ex: The workers toiled in the fields all day.
note: Also a noun meaning exhausting work.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: Willingness to accept views or behavior different from one's own.
ex: The school promotes tolerance among students.
note: Also, the ability to endure something, e.g. heat tolerance.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: To make something less intense, extreme, or forceful.
ex: The editor asked him to tone down his criticism.
note: Contrast with intensify.

label: ANALOGY PRACTICE
def: To fall over, or to cause to fall; to overthrow.
ex: The strong wind toppled several old trees in the park.
note: Often used for removing leaders from power.

label: READING
def: To become known, or to turn out.
ex: It transpired that the letter was a forgery.
note: Also used loosely to mean happen.

label: ANALOGY PRACTICE
def: A slight shaking movement, especially of the ground.
ex: A small tremor was felt before the earthquake.
note: A weaker degree of an earthquake.

label: ANALOGY PRACTICE
def: To flow slowly in a thin stream.
ex: Water trickled down the cave wall.
note: Weaker than flow; contrast with gush.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: Of little value or importance.
ex: They argued over a trivial detail.
note: Related noun: trivia.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: Using power in a cruel and unfair way.
ex: The tyrannical ruler jailed all his critics.
note: Related nouns: tyrant, tyranny.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: Done without official permission.
ex: Unauthorized entry to the lab is forbidden.
note: British spelling: unauthorised.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: Clear and allowing only one interpretation.
ex: Her answer was an unequivocal no.
note: Opposite: equivocal or ambiguous; adverb: unequivocally.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: To suddenly release a strong force or feeling.
ex: The decision unleashed a wave of protests.
note: Literally, to free a dog from its leash.

label: ANALOGY PRACTICE
def: To free from twists or knots; to make clear.
ex: It took an hour to untangle the fishing line.
note: Figuratively, to sort out a confusing problem.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: To support or confirm a law, decision, or principle.
ex: The court upheld the original ruling.
note: Contrast with overturn.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: A person who wanders from place to place without a home.
ex: The vagabond slept in a different town each night.
note: Similar to wanderer or drifter.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: The supply of fresh air to a room or building.
ex: Poor ventilation made the room stuffy.
note: Verb: ventilate.

label: ANALOGY PRACTICE
def: The decision reached at the end of a trial.
ex: The jury delivered its verdict after two days.
note: The final result of a trial, as a score is of a game.

label: READING
def: Careful watchfulness for danger or difficulty.
ex: Constant vigilance helped the guards prevent theft.
note: Adjective: vigilant.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: Absolutely necessary or essential.
ex: Water is vital for all living things.
note: Also, full of energy; noun: vitality.

label: READING
def: A bet, or to bet.
ex: He placed a small wager on the race.
note: Can be used as a noun or a verb.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: A soft substance, as in candles, that melts when heated.
ex: The candle wax dripped onto the table.
note: As a verb, to grow, as in the moon waxing and waning.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: Worth the time, money, or effort spent.
ex: Volunteering at the shelter proved a worthwhile experience for her.
note: Contrast with pointless.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: To produce a result or crop; also, to give way.
ex: The careful experiment yielded some very surprising results.
note: Also, to surrender: to yield to pressure.

label: ANALOGY PRACTICE
def: A scientist who studies animals.
ex: The zoologist observed the gorillas for months.
note: Field: zoology, as a botanist studies plants.
